usage_boundary: This is a generic New Zealand market baseline. It is not evidence of the subject company's performance, market share, equity value, enterprise value or addressable market. Sector monetary measures are broad nominal turnover proxies and must be read with their stated industry boundary.

economy_summary.headline: Activity is recovering, but the June fuel shock has lifted headline inflation and interrupted the easing cycle.
economy_summary.narrative: New Zealand real GDP expanded 0.8% in the March 2026 quarter and was 0.8% higher than a year earlier. Annual CPI inflation then rose to 4.1% in the June 2026 quarter, with petrol and diesel the dominant contributors; excluding those fuels, annual CPI rose 2.9%. The Reserve Bank increased the OCR to 2.50% on 8 July 2026. Net migration has improved from its 2025 lows but remains well below the exceptional gains of 2023-24, while the provisional population reached 5.361 million at 31 March 2026. The unemployment rate was 5.3% in the March 2026 quarter.
economy_summary.valuation_implications: The recovery in activity can support revenue expectations, but higher near-term inflation and funding costs warrant caution in nominal growth, working-capital and discount-rate assumptions. Forecasts should separate volume, price and fuel-sensitive effects rather than extrapolating headline inflation.
economy_summary.credit_implications: Borrowers face a mixed environment: improving activity and migration can support demand, while fuel, electricity, rates and interest costs can pressure margins and debt service. Lenders should test pricing pass-through, liquidity headroom and coverage at both higher funding costs and lower EBITDA.

logistics.interpretation: Nominal sales increased over the latest four quarters, indicating a broad operating market with positive current-price growth.
logistics.limitations: The source boundary is broader than towing, recovery, freight or logistics sub-sectors and includes inter-industry sales. It is not addressable market, market share or company value.

construction.interpretation: The latest quarter improved, but four-quarter nominal sales remained below the preceding four quarters.
construction.limitations: This broad construction boundary combines residential, commercial, civil and trade activity. It is not a measure of the subject company's market.

retail.interpretation: Broad nominal retail sales strengthened through the latest four quarters.
retail.limitations: The industry boundary includes multiple retail formats and does not adjust for inflation, channel mix or the subject company's product category.

hospitality.interpretation: Nominal accommodation and food-service sales increased over the latest four quarters.
hospitality.limitations: The boundary combines accommodation and food services and does not distinguish tourism, venue, geographic or format differences.

manufacturing.interpretation: Manufacturing nominal sales improved across the latest four-quarter period.
manufacturing.limitations: Manufacturing contains diverse sub-industries with different input costs, export exposure, capital intensity and margins.

professional_services.interpretation: Nominal professional-services sales increased over the latest four quarters.
professional_services.limitations: The source combines professional, scientific and technical activities and is wider than any individual advisory or technical niche.

early_childhood_education_and_care.interpretation: The sector comprised 4,390 licensed services serving 193,033 children with 33,712 teaching staff. Education-and-care occupancy was 82%.
early_childhood_education_and_care.limitations: These are structural counts, not revenue, addressable market or market value. The broad Business Financial Data education-and-training series is retained only as a low-fit directional comparator.

broad_comparator.note: Do not present this broad comparator as the size of the ECE market.

import_distribution.interpretation: Broad nominal wholesale-trade sales increased strongly over the latest four quarters.
import_distribution.limitations: Wholesale trade is a broad proxy for import distribution and includes domestic wholesale activity. Annual goods imports of NZ$87.8 billion in the year ended June 2026 provide additional context, not a directly additive market measure.
